run.question:
Alertmanager alert NoRequestsReceived (severity critical) is firing for service otel-demo/accounting since 2026-11-26T03:49:23Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The NoRequestsReceived alert fires for otel-demo/accounting because Deployment otel-demo/accounting is scaled to zero replicas, so no accounting pod exists and no accounting spans (its only 'requests', consumed Kafka order messages) are produced. The Deployment's own object shows spec.replicas 0 and no ready/available replicas, its only ReplicaSet accounting-7694cf945c has desired and actual replicas 0, and otel-demo events record Deployment accounting 'Scaled down replica set accounting-7694cf945c from 1 to 0', ReplicaSet 'Deleted pod: accounting-7694cf945c-7pt4s' and the pod's 'Stopping container accounting' at 2026-11-26T03:43:29Z. kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{deployment="accounting"} moved 1 -> 0 between the 03:43:23Z and 03:44:23Z samples, and accounting's span rate decayed from 1.9615/s (03:42:23Z sample) to 0 by the 03:49:23Z sample and stayed 0; at 03:50:00Z accounting was the only non-excluded service with a zero OK/UNSET span rate while checkout, email, payment, fraud-detection and frontend kept serving. Accounting was healthy up to its deletion (37 sampled spans on 'order-consumed', 'receive orders' and 'astronomy_db' between 03:36:24Z and 03:36:45Z with no error rows). What wrote replicas=0 is not observable with the available sources, which is a gap.

claims.text: Alert rule NoRequestsReceived (group opentelemetrydemo.requests) evaluates sum by (service_name, namespace) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{namespace="otel-demo",service_name!~"flagd|load-generator|chatbot|mcp",status_code=~"STATUS_CODE_UNSET|STATUS_CODE_OK"}[5m])) == 0 with duration 300s; at its 2026-11-26T03:54:23Z evaluation it was state firing for namespace=otel-demo, service_name=accounting with value 0e+00, active since 2026-11-26T03:49:23.340359131Z.

Deployment otel-demo/accounting (created 2026-11-26T03:36:03Z, helm release astronomy-shop, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-accounting, init container wait-for-kafka, env KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9092 and KAFKA_TOPIC=orders) has spec.replicas 0 with no readyReplicas/availableReplicas in its status; this zero-replica spec is why no accounting spans are produced and the NoRequestsReceived zero-rate condition holds.

otel-demo events record Deployment accounting 'Scaled down replica set accounting-7694cf945c from 1 to 0' at 2026-11-26T03:43:29Z, ReplicaSet accounting-7694cf945c 'Deleted pod: accounting-7694cf945c-7pt4s' at 03:43:29Z, and pod accounting-7694cf945c-7pt4s 'Stopping container accounting' at 03:43:29Z; the same pod had been scheduled and started between 03:36:03Z and 03:36:23Z.

ReplicaSet accounting-7694cf945c is controlled by Deployment accounting and currently has spec.replicas 0 and status.replicas 0, so the accounting ownership chain Deployment -> ReplicaSet -> Pod ends with no pod.

The pod listing for namespace otel-demo returned 25 pods and none of them belongs to accounting; every listed otel-demo component pod is Running and ready with restartCount 0 except that no accounting pod exists at all.

A cluster-wide query for Deployments with spec.replicas==0 returned exactly one object, namespace otel-demo name accounting (created 2026-11-26T03:36:03Z); in the otel-demo deployment table every other Deployment shows 1 desired and 1 ready/available replica.

kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="otel-demo",deployment="accounting"} was 1 at the samples 03:37:23Z, 03:38:23Z, 03:39:23Z, 03:40:23Z, 03:41:23Z, 03:42:23Z and 03:43:23Z, and 0 at every sample from 03:44:23Z through 03:54:23Z.

sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="accounting"}[5m])) was non-zero while the accounting pod ran (1.9615/s at the 03:42:23Z sample, 1.6481/s at 03:44:23Z), fell to 0.1370/s at 03:48:23Z and was 0 at every sample from 03:49:23Z through 03:54:23Z.

Using the alert's own filter (status_code=~"STATUS_CODE_UNSET|STATUS_CODE_OK", excluding flagd, load-generator, chatbot, mcp), accounting is the only service whose rate reached 0 (0 at the 03:50:23Z, 03:52:23Z and 03:54:23Z samples) while at those same samples checkout read 6.222/s, email 1.837/s, payment 0.919/s, fraud-detection 0.926/s and frontend 41.589/s.

The 24 Services in namespace otel-demo contain no Service named accounting (services listed: ad, agent, astronomy-db, cart, chatbot, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, mcp, opamp-server, otel-collector, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping, telemetry-docs, valkey-cart); accounting is a Kafka consumer (KAFKA_TOPIC orders, KAFKA_ADDR kafka:9092), so its only requests are consumed order messages recorded as spans.

Before its pod was deleted accounting was processing orders without visible errors: 12 traces sampled in 03:36:00Z-03:45:00Z contain 37 accounting spans (12 'order-consumed', 12 'receive orders', 13 'astronomy_db', duration 939us-4.34s) with 0 error rows and no status/error tags, so the loss of requests is not explained by an accounting application error.

A flagd feature-flag fault is not the cause: every flag in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config has defaultVariant "off" (including kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure and failedReadinessProbe) and no flag targets accounting.

An upstream order-flow outage is not the cause: at 03:50:00Z checkout (6.222/s), payment (0.922/s), fraud-detection (0.929/s) and email (1.837/s) still had non-zero span rates, and accounting itself saw order traffic up to its termination at 03:43:29Z, so order production was still flowing when accounting went silent.

The scale-to-zero was an externally applied change to Deployment accounting's spec.replicas at about 03:43:29Z (for example a deliberate scale-down or fault-injection step), not an application crash and not an autoscaler action; the actor that issued it is not identifiable from the available sources.

Obtain the change/audit history for the patch that set Deployment otel-demo/accounting spec.replicas to 0 at about 2026-11-26T03:43:29Z and confirm with the environment owner whether that scale-down was intended; if it was not, restoring replicas to 1 is the action that would let accounting consume orders again (advisory only, nothing was changed here).

gaps: The change_history integration is not available, so who or what set Deployment otel-demo/accounting spec.replicas=0 and the exact application time are unknown; the Deployment's managedFieldsSummary shows only manager helm Apply at 2026-11-26T03:36:03Z and manager kube-controller-manager status Update at 03:43:29Z, with no separate entry for the replica change.

Pod accounting-7694cf945c-7pt4s was deleted at 03:43:29Z and no longer exists, so its application logs, container exit code and last termination reason could not be read; a shutdown-time application error remains unchecked.
A query for horizontalpodautoscalers in otel-demo returned zero objects at query time, so no HPA is configured for accounting in this namespace; that result only shows the query matched nothing.
A query for resourcequotas in otel-demo returned zero objects at query time, so quota exhaustion was not found by that query; again this only shows the query matched nothing.

A query for endpoints filtered on name matching 'accounting' returned status no_data (zero objects), so whether an accounting Endpoints object existed at the time of the incident is unknown; only the Service list was confirmed to have no accounting entry.

Trace-based rates are only observable from about 03:37-03:38Z onward (otel-demo Deployments and their series start at 03:36:03Z), so there is no pre-03:36 baseline and no earlier comparable period for accounting in this window.

The Jaeger trace view was marked incomplete ('backend returned as many traces as requested; more may exist'), and it covered only 03:36:00Z-03:45:00Z, so accounting span content after 03:45Z and outside the sample is unknown.
No accounting pod existed at query time, so pod-level signals other than the recorded Normal events (Evicted/OOMKilled, container last state) could not be inspected for the deleted pod.
next_steps: Pull Kubernetes audit logs or the platform change history for Deployment otel-demo/accounting around 2026-11-26T03:43:29Z to identify the client or user that patched spec.replicas to 0.
Confirm with the environment owner whether the accounting scale-to-zero is an intended fault-injection step for this scenario, and restore replicas only if it is not.

After any restore, verify accounting resumes producing order-consumed spans and that kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{deployment="accounting"} returns to 1 and the NoRequestsReceived alert clears.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
